prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No modern bridge is designed for, or demonstrated to reach, a thousand years without major repair, so the Main KPI (amended by Rahul on 6 November 2026 to 1,000 bridges built in total) is unmet. The longest specified design life found is 300 years for Brisbane's Gateway Bridge, using duplex stainless rebar in splash zones (https://assda.asn.au/blog/69-stainless-integral-to-bridges-300-year-design-life); the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge was built to 120 years (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong%E2%80%93Zhuhai%E2%80%93Macau_Bridge), and UHPC footbridges to about 100 years (https://iastatedigitalpress.com/uhpc/article/9717/galley/9761/view). Steel-free precast masonry arches aim at centuries but no 1,000-year design claim was found (https://www.asme.org/topics-resources/content/precast-masonry-arch-bridge-lasts-centuries), and Roman-style self-healing concrete is lab-stage (https://news.mit.edu/topic/infrastructure?page=3&type=2). Honest limit: Roman masonry arches show 2,000-year life is physically possible, so unreinforced-arch replication is known; a 1,000-year life cannot be verified within the project and needs an agreed design-basis proof.
